88:1: Interpretation of Surah Al-Ghashiyah It was narrated from An-Nu'man ibn Bashir that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High and Al-Ghashiyah in the Eid prayer and on Fridays. Imam Malik narrated from Damrah ibn Sa'id from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah that Ad-Dahhak ibn Qays asked An-Nu'man ibn Bashir: “What did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recite on Fridays besides Surat Al-Jumu'ah?” He said: Have you received the hadith of Al-Ghashiyah? Abu Dawud narrated it from Al-Qa'nabi and An-Nasa'i from Qutaybah, both of them from Malik with this same chain of transmission. Muslim and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah from Damrah ibn Sa'id with this same chain of transmission. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful al-Ghashiyah 88:One of the names of the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said that it will cover and engulf the people. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed by a woman reciting, Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming Event? So he stood listening and said, Yes, it has come to me. And the words of God, Some faces that Day will be humbled mean, humbled. Qatadah said this. Ibn Abbas said: They will be humbled, but their deeds will not benefit them. And the words of God, Working and weary mean that she has done a lot of work and been tired in it, and she will be burned on the Day of Resurrection in a blazing Fire. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Barqani said: Ibrahim bin Muhammad Al-Muzaki told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Sarraj told us, Harun bin Abdullah told us, Sayyar told us, Jaafar told us: I heard Abu Imran Al-Joni say: Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, passed by a monk’s monastery. He said: He called out to him, O monk, and he looked out. Umar began to look at him and cry. So it was said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, what makes you cry about this? He said: I remembered the words of God Almighty in His Book: Working tirelessly, * She will be burned in a blazing Fire. And that is what made me cry. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Abbas said: Working and harassing the Christians. Ikrimah and As-Suddi said: Working in this world with sins and harassing in the Fire with torment and destruction. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They will be burned in a blazing Fire meaning very hot. They will be given to drink from a boiling spring meaning its heat and boiling have reached the end. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and As-Suddi. And the statement of God: They will have no food except from Dharee’, Ali bin Abi Talhah said: Ibn Abbas: It is a tree from fire. Saeed bin Jubayr said: It is Zaqqum, and it was narrated from him that it refers to stones. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Abu Al-Jawza’ and Qatadah said: It is Shabraq. Qatadah said: The Quraysh call it Shabraq in the spring and Dharee’ in the summer. Ikrimah said: It is a thorny tree that grows on the ground. Al-Bukhari said: Mujahid said: Ad-Dhari’ is a plant called Shabraq. The people of Hijaz call it Ad-Dhari’ when it dries, and it is poison. Muammar said on the authority of Qatada: They will have no food except from Ad-Dhari’, meaning that it is the Shabraq that when it dries, it is called Ad-Dhari’. Sa’id said on the authority of Qatada: They will have no food except from Ad-Dhari’, which is one of the worst, most disgusting and most vile foods. God Almighty said: It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger, meaning that no purpose is achieved by it, and no harm is warded off by it.

88:8: When He mentioned the state of the wretched, He followed it up by mentioning the blessed, saying: Some faces on that Day meaning on the Day of Resurrection will be blissful meaning they will know the bliss therein and that is what they achieved through their efforts. Sufyan said: Being pleased with their efforts meaning they were pleased with their work. And the Almighty’s statement: In a lofty Garden meaning elevated and splendid in the upper rooms, secure. Therein you will hear no idle talk meaning no idle talk will be heard in the Garden in which they are, as the Almighty said: “Therein they will hear no idle talk, but only, ‘Peace,’” and the Almighty said: “Therein they will hear no idle talk or sin, but only, ‘Peace, peace.’” Therein is a flowing spring meaning, flowing. This is an indefinite noun in the context of affirmation, and what is meant by it is not a single spring, but rather this is a genus, meaning there are flowing springs in it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read to Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman, who told us: Asad bin Musa told us, Ibn Thauban told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Qurrah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Damrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The rivers of Paradise gush forth from beneath hills - or from beneath mountains - of musk. “Therein are raised couches,” meaning high, soft, with many beds, and fish raised upon them are the houris. They said: So when a friend of God wants to sit upon those raised couches, they will be humbled before him. And cups placed, meaning drinking vessels prepared and set aside for whoever among their owners wants them. And cushions lined up. Ibn Abbas said: Cushions are pillows. This is what Ikrimah, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, Ath-Thawri and others said. And the Almighty’s statement: And carpets spread out. Ibn Abbas said: Carpets are rugs. This is what Ad-Dahhak and others said. The meaning of scattered is here and there for whoever wants to sit on them. He mentioned here this hadith narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud: Amr ibn Uthman told us, my father told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muhajir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak Al-Ma'afari, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, Kurayb told me that he heard Usamah ibn Zayd say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Is there anyone who prepares himself for Paradise? Indeed, Paradise is without danger. By the Lord of the Kaaba, it is a shining light, swaying basil, a lofty palace, a flowing river, ripe fruit, a beautiful wife, many garments, and a permanent residence in a sound house, with fruits and greenery, joy and comfort, in a high and splendid place?" They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. God’s prayers and peace be upon him, we are the ones who are ready for it. He said: Say, God willing. The people said: God willing. It was narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Al-Abbas bin Othman Al-Dimashqi on the authority of Al-Walid bin Muslim on the authority of Muhammad bin Muhajir on his authority.

88:17: God the Almighty says, commanding His servants to look at His creations, which demonstrate His power and greatness: Do they not then look at the camels - how they are created? They are an amazing creation and their composition is strange. They are extremely strong and powerful, yet they are gentle with heavy loads and submit to the weak leader. They are eaten, their fur is used, and their milk is drunk. They were alerted to this because the majority of the Arabs’ animals were camels. Shuraih the judge used to say, Let us go out so that we may look at the camels - how they were created, and at the sky - how it was raised! That is, how God the Almighty raised it above the earth in this great way, as God the Almighty said: Have they not looked at the sky above them - how We constructed it and adorned it and it has no rifts? “And at the mountains - how they were erected?” That is, they were made erect, for they are firm and firm so that the earth would not shake with its people. He placed in it what He did of benefits and minerals. And at the earth - how it was spread out! That is, how it was extended, spread out, and smoothed out. So the Bedouin was alerted to the evidence of what he saw of his camel that he was riding, the sky above his head, the mountain in front of him, and the earth beneath him, on the power of the Creator and Maker of that, and that He is the Great Lord, the Creator, the Owner, the Disposer, and that He is the God who is not worthy of worship other than Him. Thus, Dhimam swore in his question to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as narrated by Imam Ahmad, where he said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Sulayman bin Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: We were forbidden to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about anything, so we were pleased that a wise man from the desert would come and ask him, and we would listen. A man from the desert came and said: O Muhammad, your messenger came to us and claimed that you claim that God sent you. He said: He has spoken the truth. He said: So who created the heaven? He said: God. He said: So who created the earth? He said: God. He said: So who erected these mountains and placed in them what He placed? He said: God. He said: So by the One Who created the heaven and the earth and erected these mountains, did God send you? He said: Yes. He said: And your messenger claimed that we have to perform five prayers during the day and night? He said: He has spoken the truth. He said: So by the One Who sent you, did God command you to do this? He said: Yes. He said: And your messenger claimed that we have to pay zakat on our wealth? He said: He has spoken the truth. He said: So by the One Who sent you, did God command you to do this? He said: Yes. He said: And your messenger claimed that we have to perform Hajj to the House for those who can afford it. He said: He has spoken the truth. He then turned away and said: By the One Who sent you with the truth, I will not add anything to them nor subtract anything from them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If he has spoken the truth, they will enter Paradise. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Amr al-Naqad on the authority of Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, and al-Bukhari included it in his chain of transmission, and al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of al-Layth ibn Sa’d on the authority of Sa’id al-Maqburi on the authority of Sharik ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Namr on the authority of Anas, with it in full. He said at the end of it: And Dimam ibn Tha’labah, the brother of Banu Sa’d ibn Bakr, informed us. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Ishaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Ja’far narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, often used to narrate about a woman in the pre-Islamic period who was on the top of a mountain with her young son, tending sheep. Her son said to her: ‘O mother, who created you?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created my father?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created me?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created the heaven?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created the earth?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created the mountain?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created these sheep?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Then I hear God’s affair,’ and he threw himself down from the mountain.” It was cut off. Ibn Omar said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, often told us this. Ibn Dinar said: Ibn Omar often told us this. Its chain of transmission is weak, and this Abdullah bin Jaafar is the Madani. His son, Imam Ali bin Madani, and others weakened him. And the Almighty said: “So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them.” That is, remind the people, O Muhammad, of what you were sent to them with. For upon you is only the message, and upon Us is the reckoning. That is why He said: You are not a controller over them. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others said: And you are not a compeller over them. That is, you will not create faith in their hearts. Ibn Zayd said: You are not the one who compels them to believe. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ narrated to us from Sufyan from Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ So when they say it, their blood and wealth are protected from me except for a right, and their reckoning is with God, the Almighty and Majestic.’” Then he recited: “So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them.” This is how Muslim narrated it in the Book of Faith, and at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa’i in the Book of Tafsir in their Sunans from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Sa’id ath-Thawri with this addition. This hadith is included in the two Sahihs from the narration of Abu Hurayrah without mentioning this verse. And the Almighty’s saying: Except for he who turns away and disbelieves meaning he turns away from working with its pillars and disbelieves in the truth with his heart and tongue. This is like the Almighty’s saying: So he neither believed nor prayed, but lied and turned away. And for this reason He said: Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment. Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah told us, Layth told us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Ali ibn Khalid, that Abu Umamah al-Bahili passed by Khalid ibn Yazid ibn Mu’awiyah and asked him about the softest word he had heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Does not all of you enter Paradise except he who strays from God as a camel strays from its family?’” Imam Ahmad was the only one to narrate it. This Ali ibn Khalid was mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of his father, and he did not add anything to what is here. He narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah and from him Sa’id ibn Abi Hilal. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, to Us is their return means: their return and their turning back. Then upon Us is their account means We will hold them accountable for their deeds and reward them for them, if they do not find it. Good, then good, and if evil, then evil. That is, how God the Almighty raised it above the earth in this great way, as God the Almighty said: Have they not looked at the sky above them - how We constructed it and adorned it and it has no rifts? “And at the mountains - how they were erected?” That is, they were made erect, for they are firm and firm so that the earth would not shake with its people. He placed in it what He did of benefits and minerals. And at the earth - how it was spread out! That is, how it was extended, spread out, and smoothed out. So the Bedouin was alerted to the evidence of what he saw of his camel that he was riding, the sky above his head, the mountain in front of him, and the earth beneath him, on the power of the Creator and Maker of that, and that He is the Great Lord, the Creator, the Owner, the Disposer, and that He is the God who is not worthy of worship other than Him. Thus, Dhimam swore in his question to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as narrated by Imam Ahmad, where he said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Sulayman bin Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: We were forbidden to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about anything, so we were pleased that a wise man from the desert would come and ask him, and we would listen. A man from the desert came and said: O Muhammad, your messenger came to us and claimed that you claim that God sent you. He said: He has spoken the truth. He said: So who created the heaven? He said: God. He said: So who created the earth? He said: God. He said: So who erected these mountains and placed in them what He placed? He said: God. He said: So by the One Who created the heaven and the earth and erected these mountains, did God send you? He said: Yes. He said: And your messenger claimed that we have to perform five prayers during the day and night? He said: He has spoken the truth. He said: So by the One Who sent you, did God command you to do this? He said: Yes. He said: And your messenger claimed that we have to pay zakat on our wealth? He said: He has spoken the truth. He said: So by the One Who sent you, did God command you to do this? He said: Yes. He said: And your messenger claimed that we have to perform Hajj to the House for those who can afford it. He said: He has spoken the truth. He then turned away and said: By the One Who sent you with the truth, I will not add anything to them nor subtract anything from them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If he has spoken the truth, they will enter Paradise. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Amr al-Naqad on the authority of Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, and al-Bukhari included it in his chain of transmission, and al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of al-Layth ibn Sa’d on the authority of Sa’id al-Maqburi on the authority of Sharik ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Namr on the authority of Anas, with it in full. He said at the end of it: And Dimam ibn Tha’labah, the brother of Banu Sa’d ibn Bakr, informed us. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Ishaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Ja’far narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, often used to narrate about a woman in the pre-Islamic period who was on the top of a mountain with her young son, tending sheep. Her son said to her: ‘O mother, who created you?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created my father?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created me?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created the heaven?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created the earth?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created the mountain?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Who created these sheep?’ She said: ‘God.’ He said: ‘Then I hear God’s affair,’ and he threw himself down from the mountain.” It was cut off. Ibn Omar said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, often told us this. Ibn Dinar said: Ibn Omar often told us this. Its chain of transmission is weak, and this Abdullah bin Jaafar is the Madani. His son, Imam Ali bin Madani, and others weakened him. And the Almighty said: “So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them.” That is, remind the people, O Muhammad, of what you were sent to them with. For upon you is only the message, and upon Us is the reckoning. That is why He said: You are not a controller over them. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others said: And you are not a compeller over them. That is, you will not create faith in their hearts. Ibn Zayd said: You are not the one who compels them to believe. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ narrated to us from Sufyan from Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ So when they say it, their blood and wealth are protected from me except for a right, and their reckoning is with God, the Almighty and Majestic.’” Then he recited: “So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them.” This is how Muslim narrated it in the Book of Faith, and at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa’i in the Book of Tafsir in their Sunans from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Sa’id ath-Thawri with this addition. This hadith is included in the two Sahihs from the narration of Abu Hurayrah without mentioning this verse. And the Almighty’s saying: Except for he who turns away and disbelieves meaning he turns away from working with its pillars and disbelieves in the truth with his heart and tongue. This is like the Almighty’s saying: So he neither believed nor prayed, but lied and turned away. And for this reason He said: Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment. Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah told us, Layth told us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Ali ibn Khalid, that Abu Umamah al-Bahili passed by Khalid ibn Yazid ibn Mu’awiyah and asked him about the softest word he had heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Does not all of you enter Paradise except he who strays from God as a camel strays from its family?’” Imam Ahmad was the only one to narrate it. This Ali ibn Khalid was mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of his father, and he did not add anything to what is here. He narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah and from him Sa’id ibn Abi Hilal. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, to Us is their return means: their return and their turning back. Then upon Us is their account means We will hold them accountable for their deeds and reward them for them, if they do not find it. Good, then good, and if evil, then evil. The last interpretation of Surat Al-Ghashiyah, and praise and thanks be to God.
